title: SK Hynix: "First 3D DRAM product aims for mass production starting from 100 layers, within 4~5 years"
gist: Forum repost of a TheElec report: SK Hynix Distinguished Engineer Choi Kang-sik said SK Hynix targets 3D DRAM mass production within 4-5 years (commercialization around 2031), with a first product of 100 stacked cell layers achievable on current equipment, while 200-300+ layers need dedicated tools. SK Hynix is pursuing a selector structure, 3D NAND etch reuse, and IGZO channels, which Choi called a potential game changer if reliability is solved.

insights.claim: SK Hynix expects 3D DRAM to be commercialized around 2031, with Distinguished Engineer Choi Kang-sik stating a goal of mass production within the next 4-5 years.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: 3D DRAM is a 2030s inflection, not near-term; memory capex and tool mix shift toward vertical stacking later this decade.
insights.quote: We are developing 3D DRAM with the goal of mass production within the next 4~5 years.

insights.claim: According to SK Hynix, about 75 layers of 3D DRAM cells are needed to match the integration level of current 10nm-class DRAM, and its first 3D DRAM product will start at 100 layers.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Sets the benchmark for when 3D DRAM becomes density-competitive with planar DRAM.
insights.quote: To achieve an integration level similar to the current 10nm-class DRAM, about 75 layers of cells must be stacked
insights.locator: Choi DE said, "To achieve an integration level

insights.claim: SK Hynix says a first 100-layer 3D DRAM can be built with current equipment, but 200-300 layers and above will require development of dedicated equipment, and long term it is considering 1,000+ layers using multi-stack and hybrid bonding techniques from 3D NAND.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Dedicated equipment for high-layer 3D DRAM and hybrid bonding is a future equipment-vendor opportunity to monitor.
insights.locator: Choi DE said that the first product's level of floors

insights.claim: SK Hynix has fabricated 3D DRAM cells to verify operating characteristics and reports refresh behavior at a level similar to existing DRAM.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Early cell-level validation de-risks the roadmap somewhat, though product-level yield remains unproven.
insights.locator: He also revealed that SK Hynix fabricated 3D DRAM cells

insights.claim: DRAM is moving to 3D because miniaturization has hit its limit: shrinking cell area reduces capacitor charge storage and increases leakage current and resistance, whereas stacking cells vertically addresses charge issues while increasing integration.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Planar DRAM scaling limits underpin the long-term case for 3D DRAM process and tool transitions.
insights.locator: The reason for converting DRAM to a 3D structure

insights.claim: 3D DRAM, which stacks memory cells vertically, is a different technology from HBM (which stacks multiple DRAM chips) and from 3D stacked DRAM placed on top of logic chips.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Avoid conflating 3D DRAM roadmaps with HBM demand; they are distinct product and process vectors.
insights.locator: 3D DRAM is a structure where memory cells are stacked vertically.

themes.theme: Process challenges and SK Hynix fixes

insights.claim: 3D DRAM is made by layering and etching silicon and silicon germanium (SiGe), and as layer count rises, circuit connection structures grow more complex and etching difficulty increases.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Etch and Si/SiGe layer deposition become critical enablers; relevant to etch and deposition equipment suppliers.
insights.locator: 3D DRAM is made by layering and etching silicon

insights.claim: SK Hynix proposes a 'selector' structure that operates only the necessary circuits to cut connection area and electrical load in 3D DRAM, and is considering integrating 3D NAND etching process technology to reduce cost.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: NAND process know-how transferring into DRAM could favor memory makers with strong 3D NAND etch capability.

insights.claim: SK Hynix is researching switching 3D DRAM transistor channels from silicon to IGZO (indium gallium zinc oxide), which has lower leakage and could extend data retention, though property changes caused by hydrogen and other factors remain a challenge.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Oxide-semiconductor channel materials are a watch item for memory materials and deposition suppliers.
insights.locator: They are also researching ways to switch transistor channel materials

insights.claim: SK Hynix's Choi Kang-sik said IGZO could be a game changer for 3D DRAM if its reliability is ensured.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: IGZO reliability progress would be a leading indicator for 3D DRAM viability.
insights.quote: If IGZO's reliability is ensured, it could be a game changer in 3D DRAM.
